fact_text: A third-country professional's work-based Residencia Temporal permit must be applied for from outside Chile through SERMIG's digital portal; you cannot enter as a tourist and switch to a work permit inside the country.
evidence_quote: This application for a Residencia Temporal permit must be made from outside Chile, by logging in with the account created by the applicant for these purposes

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can arrive on a tourist stamp and convert it to a work visa once hired. Actually the work-based Residencia Temporal must be applied for from outside Chile. Action: file the SERMIG application from abroad before the employee travels.

fact_text: The work-based Residencia Temporal is granted to work in a subordinate/dependent relationship with an employer domiciled in Chile (or on a formal Chilean job offer), so the permit is tied to that employer relationship.
evidence_quote: Under a subordinate or dependent relationship with an employer who has a domicile or branch office in Chile.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a Chilean work permit lets you work for anyone. Actually it is granted for a subordinate relationship with a specific Chilean-domiciled employer. Action: confirm the hiring entity has a Chilean domicile or branch before applying.

fact_text: Where the application is based on a formal job offer, SERMIG grants a 90-calendar-day Residencia Temporal permit; after entering Chile the holder has 45 days to present the signed employment contract to obtain a 1-year extension.
evidence_quote: the person will be granted a Residencia Temporal permit for a period of 90 calendar days. Once you enter the country, you will have 45 days to present the employment contract

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the initial work visa already covers a full year. Actually a job-offer-based permit is only 90 days and the signed contract must be filed within 45 days of arrival to extend it to one year. Action: have the contract signed and ready to submit within 45 days of landing.

fact_text: Holders of a Permanencia Transitoria (tourist/short-stay) permit are not allowed to perform paid work; only exceptionally can SERMIG authorise specific, occasional remunerated activities.
evidence_quote: The holders of a Permanencia Transitoria permit will not be able to engage in remunerated activities.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can start working while your paperwork is pending on a tourist entry. Actually Permanencia Transitoria holders cannot do paid work; only a rare SERMIG special authorisation allows specific occasional activity. Action: do not start paid work until the work residence permit is granted.

fact_text: Residencia Temporal is the SERMIG-granted permit for foreigners intending to live in Chile for a limited period; it is valid for up to 2 years.
evidence_quote: foreigners who intend to reside in Chile for a limited period of time, which will be valid for up to 2 years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work residence permit is open-ended. Actually Residencia Temporal is capped at up to 2 years and must be renewed or upgraded before it lapses. Action: diarise the permit expiry and plan the Residencia Definitiva application ahead of it.

fact_text: To apply for Residencia Definitiva (permanent residence), temporary residents whose applications were submitted after 14 May 2022 must have held temporary residence in Chile for at least 24 months.
evidence_quote: must have resided in the country as such for at least 24 months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed permanent residence comes quickly after arrival. Actually you generally need at least 24 months of temporary residence first. Action: treat the first two years as temporary residence and plan the definitiva filing near month 24.

fact_text: The Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros (foreigner ID card) is issued only to people who have been granted a residence permit by the Servicio Nacional de Migraciones.
evidence_quote: Todas las personas extranjeras a quienes se les haya otorgado un permiso de residencia a través del Servicio Nacional de Migraciones

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can get a Chilean ID card on arrival. Actually the cedula is only issued once SERMIG has granted a residence permit. Action: expect the ID card only after the residence permit is approved, not on entry.

fact_text: When a foreign resident registers for a RUT (tax ID needed to work, be paid and open a bank account), they must present their Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros issued by the Registro Civil.
evidence_quote: cuando la Inscripción al RUT sea efectuada por un extranjero residente en nuestro país, al momento de realizar este trámite, deberá presentar su Cédula de Identidad para Extranjeros

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a passport is enough to get a tax ID and start working. Actually a resident's RUT registration requires the foreigner ID card (cedula) from the Registro Civil. Action: sequence it residence permit then cedula then RUT.

fact_text: A foreigner with domicile or residence in Chile is, for the first three years, taxed only on Chilean-source income; after that period they are taxed on worldwide income like any resident.
evidence_quote: durante los tres primeros años de permanencia en Chile, ya que solo deberá pagar impuestos que tengan relación con las rentas que sean de origen nacional

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed Chile taxes new residents' worldwide income immediately. Actually for the first three years a resident foreigner is taxed only on Chilean-source income. Action: plan foreign-income timing around the three-year worldwide-tax threshold.
